description: The get_* and all_* query commands that return first-class design objects (nets, pins, clocks, timing arcs, library cells, debug cores) and device objects (sites, BELs, tiles, clock regions, SLRs, package pins, I/O banks), plus the option idioms (-hierarchical, -filter, -of_objects, -regexp) and helper commands (filter, current_instance, group_path, highlight/mark) that every XDC file and analysis script is built from.

tools.name: get_nets
tools.description: Return net objects from the current design, matched by name pattern, by connection to given pins/ports/cells (-of_objects), or by property filter. -hierarchical searches every level of hierarchy, -segments returns all hierarchical segments of a net (needed when the same electrical net has different names at different levels), and -top_net_of_hierarchical_group returns the top-most segment.

parameters.name: -hierarchical (-hier)
parameters.description: Search all hierarchy levels; patterns then match the full hierarchical name.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Nets connected to the given pins, ports, cells, clocks or timing paths.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Property expression, e.g. {TYPE == GLOBAL_CLOCK && ROUTE_STATUS != ROUTED}.

parameters.name: -segments
parameters.description: Return every hierarchical segment of the matching nets.

parameters.name: -top_net_of_hierarchical_group
parameters.description: Collapse hierarchical segments to the top-level net.

tools.example:
# all global clock nets
get_nets -hier -filter {TYPE == GLOBAL_CLOCK}
# the net driven by a pin, including every hierarchical alias
get_nets -segments -of_objects [get_pins u_clk/mmcm_inst/CLKOUT0]
# nets still unrouted after route_design
get_nets -hier -filter {ROUTE_STATUS == UNROUTED}
set_property MARK_DEBUG true [get_nets -hier *fifo_full*]
tools.notes: Bus bits are separate net objects named bus[3], bus[2] ...; quote patterns with brackets in braces. Net properties worth knowing: TYPE, ROUTE_STATUS, FLAT_PIN_COUNT, IS_INTERNAL, MARK_DEBUG, DONT_TOUCH.

tools.name: get_pins
tools.description: Return pin objects of cells (hierarchical or leaf), for use as start/end points in timing constraints and as the objects that create_generated_clock, set_case_analysis, set_disable_timing and set_max_delay act on. -leaf drops hierarchical pins and returns the leaf-cell pins actually connected, and -of_objects selects the pins of given cells or nets.

parameters.name: -leaf
parameters.description: Return leaf-primitive pins only, skipping hierarchical pins.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Pins belonging to cells or connected to nets.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Common properties: DIRECTION (IN/OUT), REF_PIN_NAME, IS_CLOCK, IS_LEAF, SETUP_SLACK.

parameters.name: -include_replicated_objects
parameters.description: Also match pins on replicated cells created by phys_opt_design.

tools.example:
# clock pins of every register in a hierarchy
get_pins -of_objects [get_cells -hier -filter {PRIMITIVE_GROUP == REGISTER}] -filter {REF_PIN_NAME == C}
# leaf loads of a hierarchical output pin
get_pins -leaf -of_objects [get_nets u_core/data_out]
set_case_analysis 0 [get_pins u_clkmux/S]
set_max_delay -datapath_only 5.0 -from [get_pins sync_src_reg/C] -to [get_pins sync_dst_reg/D]
tools.notes: Pin names are cell/pin (e.g. u_fifo/wr_ptr_reg[3]/Q); REF_PIN_NAME is the primitive pin name without the instance path. Prefer pins over cells in timing exceptions when only one edge or one output is meant.

tools.name: get_clocks
tools.description: Return clock objects (primary, generated, auto-derived and virtual) by name pattern, by the pins/nets/ports they propagate through (-of_objects), or by property such as IS_GENERATED or PERIOD. It is the argument type expected by set_clock_groups, set_input_delay -clock, set_multicycle_path -start/-end and report_timing -group.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Clocks that reach the given objects; used to find the clock name on an MMCM output pin.

parameters.name: -include_generated_clocks
parameters.description: Add generated clocks derived from the matched master clocks.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: PERIOD, IS_GENERATED, IS_VIRTUAL, IS_USER_GENERATED, SOURCE_PINS, MASTER_CLOCK.

tools.example:
# all clocks faster than 200 MHz
get_clocks -filter {PERIOD < 5.0}
# clock arriving at a register
get_clocks -of_objects [get_pins u_rx/data_reg[0]/C]
set_clock_groups -asynchronous \
  -group [get_clocks -include_generated_clocks sys_clk] \
  -group [get_clocks -include_generated_clocks gt_rxclk]
tools.notes: Auto-derived clock names come from the MMCM/PLL output net (e.g. clk_out1_clk_wiz_0); report_clocks lists all names. get_generated_clocks is the same query restricted to generated clocks.

tools.name: get_generated_clocks
tools.description: Return only generated clock objects (user-created with create_generated_clock or auto-derived from MMCM/PLL/BUFGCE_DIV). Handy for scripting clock-group constraints or for renaming derived clocks with -of_objects on the generating pin.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Generated clocks propagating through the given pins/nets.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: e.g. {MASTER_CLOCK == sys_clk} or {IS_USER_GENERATED == 1}.

tools.notes: Renaming an auto-derived clock is done with create_generated_clock -name <new> [get_pins <mmcm>/CLKOUT0] with no other options, which keeps the auto-derived relationship.

tools.name: get_sites
tools.description: Return device site objects (SLICE_X0Y0, RAMB36_X1Y10, DSP48E2_X2Y3, IOB_X0Y5, MMCME4_ADV_X0Y0, GTHE4_CHANNEL_X0Y4 ...) by name, by range (-range), by containing tile/clock region/Pblock/package pin (-of_objects) or by property. Sites are the targets of LOC constraints, Pblock ranges and place_cell, and they are what the Device window shows when you hover over the fabric.

parameters.name: -range
parameters.description: Two site names giving a rectangular range, e.g. {SLICE_X0Y0 SLICE_X9Y9}.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Sites inside the given tiles, clock regions, Pblocks or SLRs, or the site a cell is placed on.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: SITE_TYPE, IS_USED, IS_RESERVED, CLOCK_REGION, SLR, PROHIBIT.

tools.example:
# free BRAM sites in clock region X2Y3
get_sites -of_objects [get_clock_regions X2Y3] -filter {SITE_TYPE == RAMB36 && IS_USED == 0}
# site a cell was placed on
get_sites -of_objects [get_cells u_ctrl/state_reg[0]]
# forbid placement in some sites
set_property PROHIBIT true [get_sites -range {SLICE_X0Y0 SLICE_X3Y59}]
tools.notes: Site names are family-specific; SLICEL vs SLICEM is a SITE_TYPE, not part of the name. PROHIBIT on sites is written to XDC and is the way to reserve area without a Pblock.

tools.name: get_bels
tools.description: Return Basic Element of Logic objects inside sites (LUTs, flip-flops, carry chains, MUXes, IDELAY elements, DSP sub-blocks). Used to discover the legal BEL names for a family before writing BEL constraints and to inspect which BELs a placed cell occupies.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: BELs within the given sites, or the BEL a cell sits on.

parameters.name: -include_routing_bels
parameters.description: Also return routing BELs (site muxes) rather than only logic BELs.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: TYPE (e.g. FF, LUT6, CARRY8), IS_USED, NAME.

tools.example:
get_bels -of_objects [get_sites SLICE_X20Y40] -filter {TYPE =~ *FF*}
# BEL of a placed cell
get_bels -of_objects [get_cells u_sync/meta_reg]
set_property BEL AFF [get_cells u_sync/meta_reg]
tools.notes: BEL names returned are fully qualified as SITE/BEL; the BEL property on a cell takes only the BEL part.

tools.name: get_tiles
tools.description: Return device tile objects (CLEL_R_X10Y20, INT_X10Y20, BRAM_X5Y15, DSP_X3Y10 ...), the physical grid unit that contains sites and the interconnect switch box. Used for low-level routing analysis, congestion scripting and for translating between sites, clock regions and interconnect resources.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Tiles containing the given sites or in the given clock regions/SLRs.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: TILE_TYPE, TYPE, GRID_POINT_X, GRID_POINT_Y, ROW, COLUMN.

tools.notes: Rarely needed in constraints; used by report_design_analysis scripts and Vivado's device-model exploration (get_nodes -of_objects [get_tiles ...]).

tools.name: get_clock_regions
tools.description: Return clock region objects (X0Y0 ... XnYm), the building blocks for coarse floorplanning and for interpreting clock-routing and report_clock_utilization output. Pblocks can be defined as clock-region ranges and USER_SLR_ASSIGNMENT / SLR queries build on them.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Clock regions containing the given sites/cells, or belonging to an SLR.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: ROW_INDEX, COLUMN_INDEX, SLR, NUM_SITES...

tools.example:
get_clock_regions -of_objects [get_slrs SLR1]
resize_pblock pb_a -add [get_clock_regions {X0Y2 X1Y2}]
report_clock_utilization -clock_roots_only
tools.notes: UltraScale-architecture clock regions are 60 CLBs tall and have 24 global clock tracks each; exceeding that in one region is a routing failure that report_clock_utilization exposes early.

tools.name: get_slrs
tools.description: Return super logic region objects (SLR0, SLR1, ...) of a stacked-silicon device. Combined with -of_objects it tells which SLR a cell, site or clock region is on, and it is the argument for Pblocks spanning whole dies and for report_utilization -slr style analysis.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: SLRs containing the given objects.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: SLR_INDEX, NUM_CLOCK_REGIONS, IS_MASTER.

tools.notes: Single-die parts return one SLR (SLR0). The master SLR (the one holding configuration logic) is flagged with IS_MASTER.

tools.name: get_package_pins
tools.description: Return package pin objects (AB12, H7, ...) with their bank, pin function, differential-pair partner and the site they connect to. Used in pin-assignment scripts, to look up which pins are clock-capable (IS_CLK_CAPABLE / IS_GLOBAL_CLK), to check bank membership and to map from a port to its physical pin.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Pins of an I/O bank, of a port (the assigned pin) or of a site.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: BANK, PIN_FUNC, IS_CLK_CAPABLE, IS_GLOBAL_CLK, IS_DIFFERENTIAL, DIFF_PAIR_PIN, IS_BONDED, IS_GT, IS_VREF.

tools.example:
# clock-capable pins in bank 34
get_package_pins -of_objects [get_iobanks 34] -filter {IS_CLK_CAPABLE}
# pin of a port and its differential partner
set p [get_package_pins -of_objects [get_ports clk_p]]
get_property DIFF_PAIR_PIN $p
# unbonded / power pins excluded
get_package_pins -filter {IS_BONDED && PIN_FUNC =~ IO_*}
tools.notes: PIN_FUNC encodes the datasheet function string (e.g. IO_L12P_T1_MRCC_34). Pin assignment itself is done with set_property PACKAGE_PIN on the port.

tools.name: get_iobanks
tools.description: Return I/O bank objects, the unit that shares VCCO, VREF and DCI settings. Query banks by number, by the ports/pins they contain or by properties such as BANK_TYPE (BT_HIGH_PERFORMANCE, BT_HIGH_RANGE, BT_HIGH_DENSITY), and use them for INTERNAL_VREF, DCI_CASCADE and for checking VCCO conflicts before running the I/O DRCs.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Banks that contain the given ports, package pins or sites.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: BANK_TYPE, NUM_PINS, VCCO (derived), IS_HPIO (family dependent).

tools.notes: Ports without PACKAGE_PIN have no bank yet; the I/O Planning layout's Package view groups pins per bank visually.

tools.name: get_io_standards
tools.description: Return the I/O standard objects supported by the target device (LVCMOS18, LVDS, SSTL12_DCI, POD12, HSTL_I, ...) together with properties such as VCCO, differential capability, drive/slew options and the bank types that accept them. Useful to validate constraint scripts across parts and to list legal standards for a bank before pin planning.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Standards currently assigned to the given ports or legal in the given banks.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: IS_DIFFERENTIAL, VCCO, DRIVE_STRENGTH, SLEW, IS_DCI, INPUT_VREF...

tools.notes: The list depends on the current part; open a design or set a part first.

tools.name: all_fanout
tools.description: Trace forward from pins/ports/nets through combinational logic and return every pin (or cell with -only_cells) in the transitive fanout, stopping at sequential elements unless -endpoints_only or -flat is changed. -levels limits the depth, -trace_arcs all follows clock and timing arcs too. It is the classic way to find all registers clocked by a net, all loads of a control signal or the cone reached from a reset.

parameters.name: <from_objects>
parameters.description: Starting ports, pins or nets.

parameters.name: -endpoints_only
parameters.description: Return only path endpoints (sequential data pins, output ports).

parameters.name: -only_cells
parameters.description: Return the cells instead of pins.

parameters.name: -flat
parameters.description: Return leaf-level pins, ignoring hierarchy.

parameters.name: -levels
parameters.description: Maximum number of cell levels to traverse.

parameters.name: -trace_arcs
parameters.description: timing (default: data arcs), enabled (arcs not disabled by case analysis), all (including clock arcs).

tools.example:
# every register reached by a synchronous reset within two LUT levels
all_fanout -flat -endpoints_only -only_cells -levels 2 [get_nets rst_sync]
# loads of a clock net, needed e.g. for a set_multicycle_path on a whole domain
llength [all_fanout -flat -endpoints_only [get_pins u_clk/bufg_slow/O] -trace_arcs all]
tools.notes: Slow on huge nets; prefer get_pins -of_objects [get_nets ...] -leaf when you only need direct loads. all_fanin is the mirror-image command.

tools.name: all_fanin
tools.description: Trace backward from pins/ports/nets through combinational logic to the driving startpoints (register outputs, input ports) and return the pins or cells on the way. Options mirror all_fanout: -startpoints_only, -only_cells, -flat, -levels, -trace_arcs. Use it to find which registers feed a timing endpoint, which port a signal ultimately comes from, or to build a false-path list for a debug cone.

parameters.name: <to_objects>
parameters.description: Ending pins, ports or nets.

parameters.name: -startpoints_only
parameters.description: Return only path startpoints.

parameters.name: -only_cells / -flat / -levels / -trace_arcs
parameters.description: As for all_fanout.

tools.example:
# registers that drive the failing endpoint pin
all_fanin -flat -startpoints_only -only_cells [get_pins u_alu/result_reg[15]/D]
# source of a clock net through buffers and MMCM
all_fanin -flat -startpoints_only [get_pins u_core/state_reg[0]/C] -trace_arcs all
tools.notes: Both fan tracers stop at sequential elements by default; with -trace_arcs all they also cross clock and enable arcs.

tools.name: all_inputs / all_outputs
tools.description: Return every top-level input (or bidirectional) port and every output (or bidirectional) port respectively. They are the SDC shortcuts for constraining all ports at once: default input/output delays, blanket false paths on unconstrained pins, or iterating over ports to check IOSTANDARD/PACKAGE_PIN assignments.
tools.notes: Clock ports are included in all_inputs; set_input_delay on a clock port is meaningless and should be excluded with [remove_from_collection [all_inputs] [get_ports clk]] or a get_ports -filter.

tools.name: all_clocks
tools.description: Return every clock object in the design, including generated, auto-derived and virtual clocks. Used to apply a constraint uniformly (clock uncertainty, jitter) or to loop over clocks in reporting scripts.
tools.notes: Equivalent to get_clocks with no pattern. Blanket clock uncertainty is a common over-constraint technique for timing closure; remove it before sign-off.

tools.name: all_rams / all_ffs / all_dsps / all_latches
tools.description: Family of shortcuts returning every block RAM/LUTRAM cell, every flip-flop, every DSP cell or every latch in the design. They are faster than a get_cells -hier -filter on PRIMITIVE_GROUP and are used for bulk attributes (e.g. switching activity on all BRAMs), latch detection after synthesis, or counting resources per hierarchy.
tools.example:
puts "latches: [llength [all_latches]]"   ;# should be 0 in a synchronous design
set_switching_activity -toggle_rate 20 -static_probability 0.5 [get_pins -of_objects [all_rams] -filter {REF_PIN_NAME =~ EN*}]
report_property [lindex [all_dsps] 0]
tools.notes: all_ffs includes I/O logic flops and SRL-based shift registers are not FFs. all_cpus and all_hsios exist for embedded processor and HSIO objects.

tools.name: filter
tools.description: Apply a property-based filter expression to an existing collection of objects and return the subset that matches, the same expression syntax as the -filter option of the get_* commands. Expressions combine property names, comparison operators (==, !=, <, >, =~ glob, !~), && / || and parentheses.

parameters.name: <objects>
parameters.description: Any collection returned by a get_* or all_* command.

parameters.name: <filter_expression>
parameters.description: e.g. {IS_PRIMITIVE && PRIMITIVE_TYPE =~ CLB.LUT.*} or {SETUP_SLACK < 0}.

parameters.name: -regexp
parameters.description: Treat =~ patterns as regular expressions instead of globs.

tools.example:
set regs [all_ffs]
set async_regs [filter $regs {ASYNC_REG == 1}]
set big_pblocks [filter [get_pblocks] {CELL_COUNT > 5000}]
set failing [filter [get_timing_paths -max_paths 100] {SLACK < 0}]
tools.notes: Properties available for filtering are listed by list_property <object> and report_property; boolean properties can be tested by name alone. Expressions must be in braces so Tcl does not expand them.

tools.name: current_instance
tools.description: Set (or query) the hierarchical instance that subsequent get_* queries and constraints are scoped to, so an XDC file written for a sub-module can use relative names. IP and hierarchical OOC constraints rely on it, and Vivado automatically wraps IP XDC files in current_instance calls. Calling it with no argument prints the current scope; -quiet with an empty string resets to the top.
tools.usage:
current_instance [-quiet] [<instance>]
current_instance          ;# back to top level

parameters.name: <instance>
parameters.description: Hierarchical cell to scope to; relative names are resolved from the current scope.

tools.example:
current_instance u_rx_path/u_deserializer
set_property IOB TRUE [get_cells {data_reg[*]}]
set_false_path -to [get_pins sync_reg[0]/D]
current_instance
# equivalent explicit form
set_property IOB TRUE [get_cells {u_rx_path/u_deserializer/data_reg[*]}]
tools.notes: Timing constraints inside a scoped block still refer to top-level clocks by their global names. Use get_property SCOPED_TO_CELLS on an XDC file to scope a whole file to one or more instances instead.

tools.name: group_path
tools.description: Assign timing paths to a named path group so they are reported and optimized separately, with optional -weight to bias the placer/router toward that group. Paths are selected by -from/-to/-through or by clock; -default returns them to the default group. Vivado already groups paths per destination clock; user groups are used for critical interfaces and for isolating a problem region in report_timing_summary.

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Path group name; appears as a section in timing reports and in report_timing -group.

parameters.name: -weight
parameters.description: 1 (default) or 2 for higher optimization priority.

parameters.name: -from / -to / -through
parameters.description: Path selectors, same objects as set_false_path.

parameters.name: -default
parameters.description: Move the matching paths back to the default group.

tools.example:
group_path -name pcie_user -weight 2 -to [get_cells -hier -filter {NAME =~ *pcie_user_logic*}]
report_timing -group pcie_user -max_paths 10
get_path_groups
tools.notes: Too many groups dilute optimization effort. get_path_groups lists the existing groups (clock names plus **async_default** for asynchronous paths).

tools.name: get_path_groups
tools.description: List the timing path groups in the design: one per clock, **async_default** for recovery/removal paths and any user groups created with group_path. Used to iterate report_timing per group or to check that a group_path command took effect.

parameters.name: <patterns>
parameters.description: Group names to match, default all.

tools.notes: Groups are created automatically as clocks are defined; a group disappears when its constraints are removed.

tools.name: get_lib_cells / get_lib_pins
tools.description: Query the device primitive library: get_lib_cells returns the primitive definitions available for the target part (FDRE, LUT6, RAMB36E2, DSP48E2, BUFGCE, ...) and get_lib_pins their pins with direction and function. Used to check which primitives a part supports, to script create_cell -reference in ECO flows, and to look up pin names before writing BEL/pin constraints.

parameters.name: <patterns>
parameters.description: Library-qualified names such as xilinx.com/UltraScale/FDRE or wildcard */LUT6.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: The library cell of a netlist cell, or the pins of a library cell.

parameters.name: -include_unsupported
parameters.description: Also list primitives not supported on this part.

tools.example:
get_lib_cells [get_libs]/*DSP*
get_lib_pins -of_objects [get_lib_cells [get_libs]/DSP48E2] -filter {DIRECTION == IN}
# ECO: add a register
create_cell -reference FDRE eco_reg
report_property [get_lib_cells -of_objects [get_cells eco_reg]]
tools.notes: get_libs returns the single device library (e.g. xilinx.com/UltraScale). Library cell properties include PRIMITIVE_GROUP, PRIMITIVE_SUBGROUP and NUM_PINS.

tools.name: get_timing_arcs
tools.description: Return the timing arcs (from-pin to to-pin delay relationships) of cells or between pins, with their sense, type and delays, including arcs disabled by set_disable_timing or by case analysis. Useful for understanding why a path is or is not timed, for verifying that a set_disable_timing took effect and for inspecting MUX/LUT arcs before writing exceptions.

parameters.name: -from / -to
parameters.description: Restrict arcs to those starting or ending on the given pins.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: All arcs of the given cells.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: IS_DISABLED, SENSE (positive_unate/negative_unate/...), TYPE (combinational/setup/hold/recovery/...), DELAY_MIN_RISE etc.

tools.example:
get_timing_arcs -of_objects [get_cells u_mux/clk_sel_LUT]
get_timing_arcs -filter {IS_DISABLED} -of_objects [get_cells -hier -filter {PRIMITIVE_TYPE =~ *BUFGMUX*}]
set_disable_timing -from I1 -to O [get_cells u_mux/clk_sel_LUT]
report_disable_timing
tools.notes: Arc objects print as cell/pin1-->cell/pin2. The delays are timing-corner dependent; report_timing shows the ones actually used.

tools.name: get_net_delays
tools.description: Return net-delay objects describing the routed (or estimated) delay from a net's driver to each load pin, for fast/slow corners, with the option to restrict to specific -to pins and to use -interconnect_only. Used for skew analysis on hand-routed nets, matched-length checks and for validating clock-tree delays without a full report_timing.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Nets to analyse.

parameters.name: -to
parameters.description: Only the delays to these load pins.

parameters.name: -interconnect_only
parameters.description: Exclude the driver's intrinsic delay, report the wire delay only.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: FAST_MAX, FAST_MIN, SLOW_MAX, SLOW_MIN in ps.

tools.notes: Values are in picoseconds; before route_design they are estimates. For a full slack picture use report_timing -path_type full_clock_expanded.

tools.name: get_nodes / get_pips / get_wires
tools.description: Low-level routing-resource queries: nodes are the routable wire segments, PIPs (programmable interconnect points) are the switches between them, and wires are the per-tile pieces of a node. -of_objects on a routed net returns the nodes/PIPs it uses, which is how a route is inspected, copied (set_property ROUTE / FIXED_ROUTE) or reserved (set_property IS_ROUTE_FIXED). Rarely needed outside custom routing or analysis scripts.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Routing resources used by a net, or reachable from a node/pip/tile.

parameters.name: -uphill / -downhill
parameters.description: Nodes or PIPs driving into, or driven by, the given object.

parameters.name: -flyover
parameters.description: Include nodes that pass over the tile without connecting.

tools.example:
set n [get_nets u_serdes/dq_dly]
get_nodes -of_objects $n
get_pips  -of_objects $n
# lock the route so route_design reuses it
set_property IS_ROUTE_FIXED 1 $n
get_property ROUTE $n
tools.notes: The ROUTE property string (a nested list of node names) and FIXED_ROUTE constraints are the way to make a route reproducible across runs. Node names are tile/wire, e.g. INT_X10Y20/EE2_E_BEG0.

tools.name: get_site_pins
tools.description: Return the site pins (the physical pins of a site such as SLICE_X1Y1/A6 or RAMB36_X0Y0/CLKARDCLK) that a net or a cell pin is connected to. Bridges the logical netlist (cell pins) and the physical device (nodes), and is used when writing LOCK_PINS constraints or tracing a route from a pin.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Site pins belonging to a site, connected to a net, or mapped from a cell pin.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: DIRECTION, IS_INPUT, IS_OUTPUT, IS_USED, IS_CLOCK.

tools.example:
get_site_pins -of_objects [get_pins u_ctrl/state_reg[2]/D]
get_site_pins -of_objects [get_sites SLICE_X10Y42] -filter {IS_USED}
tools.notes: A cell pin maps to a site pin only after placement; before place_design the query returns nothing.

tools.name: get_debug_cores / get_debug_ports
tools.description: Return the debug cores (ILA, VIO, dbg_hub) present in the netlist-insertion debug flow and their ports (probe0, clk, ...). Used together with create_debug_core, create_debug_port, connect_debug_port and set_property C_* to script debug insertion, and to inspect what a checkpoint already contains before implement_debug_core.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Cores owning the given ports, or ports of the given cores.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Core properties: C_DATA_DEPTH, C_NUM_OF_PROBES, C_ADV_TRIGGER; port properties: PORT_WIDTH, MATCH_TYPE.

tools.notes: The hub core dbg_hub is always present once any debug core exists; its C_CLK_INPUT_FREQ_HZ and C_ENABLE_CLK_DIVIDER properties control JTAG-to-hub timing.

tools.name: get_drc_violations / get_methodology_violations / get_cdc_violations
tools.description: Return the violation objects produced by the last report_drc, report_methodology or report_cdc run, filterable by check ID, severity or affected objects. They let scripts iterate over violations, extract the cells involved (get_cells -of_objects), decide pass/fail in CI, and generate waivers with create_waiver -of_objects.

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Name given to the report with report_drc -name / report_methodology -name; default is the last unnamed run.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: SEVERITY, CHECK, DESCRIPTION, IS_WAIVED.

tools.notes: Violation objects live only while the named report exists (delete with reset_drc / reset_methodology). Use create_waiver to suppress justified violations and report_waivers to review them.

tools.name: get_hierarchy_separator / set_hierarchy_separator
tools.description: Query or change the character used to separate hierarchy levels in object names ('/' by default). Changing it is only needed for legacy scripts written with '.' separators; the -hsc option on get_* commands does the same per query.

parameters.name: <separator>
parameters.description: Single character, typically / or .

tools.example:
puts [get_hierarchy_separator]   ;# /
get_cells -hsc . top.u_core.state_reg
set_hierarchy_separator /
tools.notes: Generated netlist names from write_verilog keep '/' escaped; do not change the separator inside XDC files that IP also reads.

tools.name: get_selected_objects / select_objects
tools.description: Bridge between the GUI selection and Tcl: get_selected_objects returns whatever is currently selected in the Device, Schematic, Netlist or Timing windows, and select_objects selects objects from Tcl so the GUI views jump to them. Used interactively to apply constraints to a hand-picked set or to inspect properties of what was clicked.

parameters.name: -add
parameters.description: Add to the existing selection rather than replacing it.

tools.example:
# pick cells in the Device window, then:
set_property IS_LOC_FIXED true [get_selected_objects]
select_objects [get_cells -hier -filter {PRIMITIVE_TYPE =~ *MMCM*}]
tools.notes: Only meaningful with the GUI open; in batch mode the selection is empty. Related: get_highlighted_objects, get_marked_objects.

tools.name: highlight_objects / mark_objects / show_objects
tools.description: GUI helpers callable from Tcl: highlight_objects colours cells, nets, sites or Pblocks in the Device and Schematic windows (-color / -color_index, -leaf_cells), mark_objects places a marker on them, and show_objects opens a Find Results style window listing the collection. They are the scripted equivalents of the right-click Highlight / Mark / Show commands and are invaluable for visualising a filter result (e.g. all cells of a failing path).
tools.usage:
highlight_objects [-color_index <1-20>] [-rgb {r g b}] [-color <name>] [-leaf_cells] [-quiet] <objects>
unhighlight_objects [-color_index <n>] [-rgb {r g b}] [-color <name>] [-leaf_cells] [<objects>]
mark_objects [-color <name>|-rgb {r g b}|-color_index <n>] <objects>
unmark_objects [<objects>]
show_objects [-name <window_name>] [-quiet] <objects>

parameters.name: -color / -rgb / -color_index
parameters.description: Colour by name (red, green, ...), RGB triple or palette index.

parameters.name: -leaf_cells
parameters.description: Highlight the leaf primitives under hierarchical cells.

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Title of the result window created by show_objects.

tools.example:
set wp [get_timing_paths -max_paths 1 -setup]
highlight_objects -color red -leaf_cells [get_cells -of_objects $wp]
mark_objects -color yellow [get_sites -of_objects [get_cells -of_objects $wp]]
show_objects -name worst_path_cells [get_cells -of_objects $wp]
unhighlight_objects
tools.notes: Highlights persist until unhighlight_objects; each colour index can be cleared separately. In batch mode these commands are accepted but do nothing.

tools.name: Query options: -hierarchical, -filter, -of_objects, -regexp, -nocase, -quiet
tools.description: Common option set shared by every get_* command. Patterns are glob-style by default (* and ?) and match the full name; -hierarchical (or -hier) searches all levels and makes patterns match hierarchical names (so *reg* is needed to match u_a/u_b/reg); -regexp switches patterns to Tcl regular expressions, -nocase ignores case; -filter applies a property expression; -of_objects pivots from one object type to a related one; -quiet suppresses the warning when nothing matches (important inside XDC files that must not fail on optional objects). Results are Tcl lists of objects and can be combined with concat, lsort -unique, remove_from_collection and the filter command.

parameters.name: -hierarchical
parameters.description: Search below the current instance; without it only the current level is searched and hierarchical patterns need explicit levels (a/b/c).

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: {PROP OP value [&& ...]} with ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=, =~ (glob), !~ ; boolean props can be named alone.

parameters.name: -of_objects
parameters.description: Related-object pivot: cells of nets, pins of cells, sites of cells, clocks of pins, nets of timing paths, etc.

parameters.name: -regexp / -nocase
parameters.description: Regular-expression and case-insensitive matching; -regexp also applies to =~ in -filter.

parameters.name: -quiet
parameters.description: No warning / empty result on no match; use in XDC when objects may not exist in every configuration.

parameters.name: -match_style ucf|sdc
parameters.description: Whether bus patterns like data[*] or data* follow UCF or SDC conventions (default sdc).

tools.example:
# clocked elements in one hierarchy, any level below it
get_cells -hier -filter {NAME =~ u_core/* && IS_SEQUENTIAL}
# case-insensitive regexp on nets
get_nets -hier -regexp -nocase {.*/axi_(aw|ar)valid$}
# pivot chains: ports -> package pins -> iobank
get_iobanks -of_objects [get_package_pins -of_objects [get_ports {dq[*]}]]
# tolerate absent objects in XDC
set_false_path -quiet -to [get_cells -quiet -hier -filter {NAME =~ *dbg_only*}]
tools.notes: Every get_* warns (CRITICAL WARNING in XDC) when a pattern matches nothing; over-broad -hier * queries on million-cell designs are slow, so narrow with -filter on PRIMITIVE_TYPE or NAME first.

tools.name: Object properties (PRIMITIVE_TYPE, IS_SEQUENTIAL, REF_NAME, LOC, ROUTE_STATUS ...)
tools.description: Every Vivado object carries read-only and settable properties that drive -filter expressions and get_property/set_property. On cells the most used are NAME, REF_NAME (module or primitive name), PRIMITIVE_TYPE (e.g. CLB.LUT.LUT6, REGISTER.SDR.FDRE, BLOCKRAM.BRAM.RAMB36E2), PRIMITIVE_GROUP (CLB, REGISTER, BLOCKRAM, DSP, CLOCK, IO, GT), IS_PRIMITIVE, IS_SEQUENTIAL, IS_BLACKBOX, LOC, BEL, IS_LOC_FIXED, IS_BEL_FIXED, DONT_TOUCH, ASYNC_REG, KEEP_HIERARCHY; on nets TYPE, ROUTE_STATUS, ROUTE, FLAT_PIN_COUNT, MARK_DEBUG; on pins DIRECTION, IS_CLOCK, IS_LEAF, SETUP_SLACK/HOLD_SLACK; on ports PACKAGE_PIN, IOSTANDARD, DRIVE, SLEW, PULLTYPE; on timing paths SLACK, REQUIREMENT, DATAPATH_DELAY, LOGIC_LEVELS, STARTPOINT_PIN, ENDPOINT_PIN, GROUP; on runs STATUS, PROGRESS, STRATEGY, STEPS.*; on files FILE_TYPE, LIBRARY, USED_IN, IS_ENABLED, IS_GLOBAL_INCLUDE.
tools.usage:
list_property <object>            ;# names
report_property <object>          ;# names, types, values
get_property <PROP> <object>
set_property <PROP> <value> <objects>

parameters.name: list_property_value
parameters.description: Enumerates the legal values of an enumerated property, e.g. list_property_value IOSTANDARD [get_ports clk].

parameters.name: reset_property
parameters.description: Restore a property to its default (removes a constraint).

tools.example:
report_property [get_cells u_core/state_reg[0]]
list_property_value FSM_ENCODING [get_cells u_core/state_reg[0]]
get_cells -hier -filter {PRIMITIVE_TYPE =~ BLOCKRAM.* && IS_LOC_FIXED}
reset_property LOC [get_cells u_core/state_reg[0]]
set_property -dict {IOSTANDARD LVCMOS18 PACKAGE_PIN AB12 SLEW FAST} [get_ports led0]
tools.notes: Property names are case-insensitive but conventionally upper case. UG912 (Vivado Properties Reference) documents each property with its legal values and the objects it applies to.

tools.name: get_designs
tools.description: Return the design objects currently open in memory (there can be several, e.g. an elaborated RTL design and an implemented run) and let scripts select one with current_design or close the others. Design properties give the part, top module, and whether it is netlist- or RTL-based.

parameters.name: -filter
parameters.description: Properties: NAME (e.g. synth_1, impl_1, rtl_1), PART, TOP.

tools.notes: Memory usage grows with each open design; close_design before opening another in batch flows.
